item.title: Meta AI launches Muse Ember, a small, efficient reasoning model
item.description:
Meta AI launches Muse Ember, a small, efficient reasoning model

Meta AI just launched Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day.

🔍 Overview

  • Smallest and most efficient model in the Claude Haiku/GPT Luna category.
  • Targeted at tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.

🧩 How it works

  • Offers six reasoning levels: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max.
  • Visual examples include six pelicans riding bicycles, with the “max” level shown and others noted as comparable to Muse Wonder (40× the price of Ember).

⚙️ Key details

Model Input price (per M tokens) Output price (per M tokens) Token limit
Muse Ember $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
GPT‑6 Luna $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
Claude Haiku 5.5 $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
Claude Fable 5.2 $8.00 $40.00 –
  • For shorter prompts Ember is priced the same as GPT‑6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5.
  • Pricing becomes less straightforward as prompts get longer; after the threshold Ember’s price sits between Luna/Haiku and Claude Fable.

📊 Efficiency metrics

  • Artificial Analysis is highlighted as a useful measure.
  • The Intelligence Index vs. Cost per Task chart places Muse Ember on the Pareto line, where improving one dimension requires sacrificing another.
  • Meta notes Ember sits on the efficiency frontier of the full Artificial Analysis leaderboard: no model scores higher for less per task.
  • The grey dot on the Pareto line (mid‑green area) represents GPT‑6.1 Terra (low), noted as worth attention.

🚀 Availability

  • Muse Ember is available now with pricing identical to GPT‑6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 for short inputs.
  • Longer prompts trigger a price threshold, positioning Ember’s cost between the low‑price models and the higher‑priced Claude Fable 5.2.

#MetaAI #MuseEmber #AIModels #Pricing #ArtificialAnalysis

Source: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember

item.title: Latency-Aware Adaptive Best-of-N Improves Test-Time Compute Efficiency
item.description:
Latency-Aware Adaptive Best-of-N Improves Test-Time Compute Efficiency

A new arXiv paper titled Latency-Aware Adaptive Best-of-$N$ introduces a two‑stage algorithm that adapts test‑time compute (TTC) based on observed latency, achieving lower cost than traditional fixed‑threshold methods.

🔍 Overview

  • Test‑time compute boosts language‑model responses by allocating extra inference computation, and the optimal amount varies by prompt.
  • Existing adaptive TTC methods stop when a quality signal exceeds a fixed threshold and measure cost by the number of generations or tokens.
  • In online serving, latency also incurs cost because it grows with server load; fixed thresholds can under‑compute when generation is fast and over‑compute when it is slow.

🧩 How It Works

  • Two‑stage adaptive algorithm for Best‑of‑$N$ sampling:
    1. Draw an initial batch of generations.
    2. Use the batch’s observed rewards and its latency to decide whether to draw a second batch and how large it should be.
  • Decision rule: draw a second batch when the first batch’s best reward is below a threshold that decreases with the first batch’s latency; server load is not measured explicitly.
  • Rewards are mapped to their values under the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the prompt’s reward distribution, allowing the same trade‑off parameters to be reused across tasks.
  • An offline regression fitted on other prompts predicts the CDF‑value distribution of the first batch’s best reward, providing a closed‑form expected improvement.

⚙️ Evaluation & Results

  • Simulated on a preference‑based alignment benchmark.
  • Cost measured as generations‑equivalent: generations plus latency, converted to generations.
  • Findings:
    • The method reaches the same reward as standard Best‑of‑$N$ at lower generations‑equivalent cost.
    • Conditioning on the measured first‑batch latency saves at least as much cost as latency‑unaware fixed‑threshold baselines.
    • Savings are larger when latency is highly variable, when latency grows with batch size, and when the second‑batch latency is highly predictable from the first.

🚀 Availability

  • The paper was submitted to arXiv on 5 Nov 2026 under the Computer Science > Computation and Language category.
  • It is part of the arXiv ecosystem, which supports community‑driven projects through initiatives such as arXivLabs.

This post summarizes the technical contributions and evaluation of the latency‑aware adaptive Best‑of‑$N$ method as described in the submitted manuscript.

#test-time-compute #latency #adaptive-sampling #AIresearch

Source: Latency-Aware Adaptive Best-of-$N$

item.title: WISE Method Optimizes Recurrent Language Model Inference via Support Exploitation
item.description:
WISE Method Optimizes Recurrent Language Model Inference via Support Exploitation

Researchers have introduced WISE (Working-set Inference with Support Exploitation), a training-free method designed to improve the efficiency of recurrent language models by optimizing how they handle global attention during inference.

🔍 Overview

Recurrent language models refine latent representations by repeatedly applying shared network blocks. However, standard inference typically recomputes global attention at every recurrent step. The developers of WISE discovered that attention support and distributions stabilize substantially earlier than attention outputs and hidden states.

🧩 How it works

WISE leverages the observation that early recurrent steps identify a sparse working set of relevant context, while subsequent steps refine representations using largely the same routing support. The method operates as follows:

  • Early Recurrence: Uses unrestricted global attention.
  • Later Recurrence: Reuses the directly discovered block-structured support.
  • Dynamic Control: Keeps recurrent depth and within-support attention computation dynamic.

⚙️ Key details

Controlled interventions indicated that recurrent discovery is necessary and that support-only reuse preserves model behavior better than more restrictive attention-reuse options. Performance metrics include:

Metric Result
Multi-hop QA Performance Largely preserves full-attention performance
Quality (2K context) Largely preserved
Quality (4K context) Measurable loss
Max Attention Speedup (4K) Up to 1.76x over native FlashAttention
Full 32-step Trajectory Speedup 1.36x

💡 Why it matters

Context scaling reveals that as context increases, working sets become increasingly sparse, leading to greater efficiency gains.

#LLM #InferenceOptimization #AttentionMechanism #RecurrentLanguageModels

Source: Attention Routing Stabilizes Early: Working-Set Inference for Recurrent Language Models
